title: Bench memo on the clipped first word
public_context: A bench memo from a fictional sound archive concerns listening copies made from historical recordings. The setting includes a technician, headphones, stored media and derivative files, and the document belongs to ordinary audio preservation and access work. It is filed with routine listening-room paperwork.
source_title: Bench memo 3 from the Marlin Sound Room
source_text:
Two readers asked why the first word on the Marlin Sound Room's listening copy sounded as if it began in the middle. The source was a wire recording of a ferry announcement, transferred to a digital file the previous month. Technician Esi Rall found a broad low-frequency hum before the announcement and applied a filter that reduced steady noise below the speaker's voice band. The filter also shortened the opening transient, which made the first consonant difficult to hear.

Rall compared three versions through the same headphones: the unfiltered transfer, the filtered copy, and a copy with the filter's threshold lowered. The unfiltered version retained the hum but preserved the first consonant. The original filtered version reduced the hum more strongly but clipped part of the consonant. Lowering the threshold restored more of the consonant while leaving a softer hum. Rall wrote that the third version was easier to follow in the bench room, but she did not call it a correction to the source.

The archive keeps the wire recording in its case, the unfiltered transfer as the preservation file, and each processed version in a separate listening folder with the filter settings attached. Rall did not overwrite the preservation file or splice a new consonant into the processed copy. She added a note to the listening description that the first consonant is less distinct in the stronger filter version. The file labels show that the announcement begins after a short leader, but no transcript identifies the speaker or gives the exact words.

A later reader asked whether the announcement was made before the ferry left or after it arrived. The memo says the recording mentions the east landing, but the phrase is partially masked by a bell and does not settle the timing. Rall recommends keeping both the unfiltered and softer-filter copies available so a listener can judge the tradeoff. She attached a settings sheet to the third version, left it in the listening folder beside the unfiltered transfer, returned the headphones to the bench drawer and initialed the memo. The settings leaf carries the date of this bench session and the technician's initials.
